prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
method MinSecondValueFirst(s: array<seq<int>>) returns (firstOfMinSecond: int)
    requires s.Length > 0
    requires forall i :: 0 <= i < s.Length ==> |s[i]| >= 2
    ensures exists i :: 0 <= i < s.Length && firstOfMinSecond == s[i][0] && 
        (forall j :: 0 <= j < s.Length ==> s[i][1] <= s[j][1])
{
    var minSecondIndex := 0;
    for i := 1 to s.Length
        invariant 0 <= i <= s.Length
        invariant 0 <= minSecondIndex < (i) + 1
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> s[minSecondIndex][1] <= s[j][1]
    {
        if s[i][1] < s[minSecondIndex][1]
        {
            minSecondIndex := i;
        }
    }
    firstOfMinSecond := s[minSecondIndex][0];
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(11,46): Error: index out of range

program.dfy(11,62): Error: index out of range

program.dfy(18,25): Error: index out of range

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant

raw_response: {"spec_element": "invariant", "proof_obligation": "bridge", "diagnosis": "The bound invariant '0 <= minSecondIndex < (i) + 1' is too weak because it allows minSecondIndex == i. Inside the loop, the next invariant indexes s[minSecondIndex][1] (line 11), and Dafny cannot prove that index is below s.Length when i == s.Length. On loop exit i == s.Length, so the invariant only gives minSecondIndex <= s.Length. That is not enough to show s[minSecondIndex][0] (line 18) is in range, nor to discharge the postcondition. In reality minSecondIndex is only ever set to values strictly less than i, so the tighter bound is both initially true (0 < 1) and preserved.", "repair": "invariant 0 <= minSecondIndex < i"}
reasoning_content: I see the bug now: the invariant bound allows minSecondIndex to equal i, which could reach s.Length and cause an out-of-range access. It should be strictly less than i instead of i+1, since with i starting at 1, minSecondIndex=0 still satisfies that tighter bound.
